model.name: Model for chlorzoxazone elimination in the liver

notes.body:
Model for chlorzoxazone elimination in the liver
Model for the hepatic metabolism of chlorzoxazone via CYP2E1 and a second, CYP2E1 independent pathway, the glucuronidation of 6-hydroxychlorzoxazone, the elimination of ethanol and the turnover of CYP2E1 encoded in SBML format.
The content of this model has been carefully created in a manual research effort.

body.p: Half-life of CYP2E1 without ethanol: about 7 hr for the unstabilized and about 37 hr for the ethanol stabilized protein in rats (Roberts1995); the activity of drinkers normalizes within about one week of withdrawal (Oneta2002, Lucas1995).

parameter.name: rate constant for chlorzoxazone import into the liver

body.p: The liver concentration at equilibrium is the concentration of the hepatic plasma over CZX_F_EX, a liver to plasma ratio of 1/1.59 = 0.627 (0.627 +- 0.062 in rats, Kim2002). The parameter is equivalent to the Km of the CYP2E1 and to the rate of the second pathway, which are fitted, and stays fixed.
The liver to plasma ratio at equilibrium, 0.221 +- 0.009 in rats (Kim2002).
Activity of CYP2E1 relative to healthy subjects (1), e.g. the inhibition by a coadministered drug; set by the experiments, not fitted.

parameter.name: rate constant of the glucuronidation of 6-hydroxychlorzoxazone

body.p: First order: the glucuronidation by UGT1A1, UGT1A6 and UGT1A9 is not saturated at the concentrations of 6-hydroxychlorzoxazone in vivo. The free 6-hydroxychlorzoxazone in plasma is 1.4-3.3 % of chlorzoxazone 0.5 hr after a microdose (Witt2016, Hohmann2019), the glucuronide is the main form in plasma and urine.
The value of LI__CZXOGLU_k is the result of the fit PK_20261020_035132__b4a12, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

The alcohol dehydrogenase has a Km of about 0.1 g/l (2.17 mM) in vivo (Holford1987). Not fitted: the blood ethanol of Wilkinson1977 does not identify it (flat profile likelihood from 0.05 to 5 mM).
Calculated from the half-life cyp2e1_thalf, kd = ln(2)/t_half.

Ethanol stabilizes CYP2E1 against its degradation. With a constant far below the hepatic ethanol of drinking the stabilization is a switch: the induction is the fraction of the day with ethanol in the liver, about 1.9-fold after weeks of 50 g ethanol a day, back to 1 within a week of abstinence (the about twofold activity of drinkers). A constant of 1 mM gives an induction of 1.3-fold only. The value is not identified by the data.
degradation rate = ln(2)/thalf
production rate = degradation rate at baseline resulting in cyp2e1 = 1.0 dimensionless
cyp2e1 is normalized to 1

The elimination of chlorzoxazone which is not the 6-hydroxylation: only 71-74 % of an oral dose are recovered as 6-hydroxychlorzoxazone in the urine (Desiraju1983, Kharasch1993), the formation clearance of 6-hydroxychlorzoxazone is 70 % of the clearance (Kharasch1993), the remaining clearance is 158-191 ml/min (Frye1998). Under disulfiram, which inactivates CYP2E1, Kharasch1993 found a "metabolic switching to an as-yet unidentified metabolite". The products are not modeled.
Catalyzed by UGT enzymes.
Ethanol elimination via alcohol dehydrogenase in the liver. Due to saturation of enzyme (ethanol > ETHEL_KM) constant rate of ethanol elimination.
Ethanol stabilizes CYP2E1, i.e., the degradation rate is reduced.
